pass_a_gloss: And next to this it is said: 'Be circumcised to your God, circumcise the foreskin of your heart.' 'Be circumcised to your God' — necessarily is added 'Be circumcised to your God.' You will understand it from the example of the sensible: they are circumcised, according to the sensible I say, not only those from circumcision according to the law of Moses, but also many others. Of the Egyptians' idols, the priests are circumcised, but that circumcision is a circumcision of idols and not a circumcision made to God; and the Jews perhaps, but certainly then it was made to God. Therefore if the word says, 'Be circumcised to your God,' having understood the literal, proceed to the tropology, so that you may find how the circumcisions are tropologized (so as to perhaps say some of them: 'We are the circumcision') — some indeed are circumcised to God, but others are over-circumcised, not to God. There are also other words beside the word of truth, beside the word of the church. Customs and the heart are circumcised as it were to say that philosophers make sober, and those from heresies make sober, and it becomes to them a circumcision. But circumcision indeed, not to God — for circumcision by a false word according to them becomes. But when according to the ecclesiastical canon, according to the intention of the wholesome teaching, social he, you are not only circumcised, but you are circumcised 'to God.' 'Be circumcised' therefore to your God, and circumcise the foreskin of your heart of yours (who does not pass over these things as clear? Therefore there is a foreskin of the heart and this must be circumcised). The one who has exacted the word in this way examines in the place: the foreskin is born with, the circumcision is acquired, and what has come from birth, this the circumcision takes away. Therefore if the word commands to take away 'the foreskin of the heart,' it must be something born together with the heart, which it calls foreskin, which must be taken away, so that one may be circumcised 'the foreskin of the heart.' If anyone understands 'we were by nature children of wrath, as also the others,' if anyone understands 'the body of humiliation' in which we were born, if anyone understands 'no one is clean from filth, not even if one day were his life,' — but the months of his are countable, he will see in what manner we were born with uncleanness and foreskin of our hearts.

pass_b_english: And next to this it is said: 'Be circumcised to your God; circumcise the foreskin of your heart.' (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jer 4:4) 'Be circumcised to your God'—necessarily is added 'to your God.' You will understand it from the sensible example. According to the sensible I say: not only those of the circumcision according to Moses' (Ephesians 2:3) law are circumcised, but many others also. The priests of the Egyptians' idols are circumcised, but that circumcision is circumcision to idols and is not circumcision done to God. The Jews' circumcision, perhaps—and certainly then—was done to God.

So when the word says, 'Be circumcised to your God,' understand the saying and move also to the figurative reading, so that you find how, among figurative circumcisions (so that some of them might even say, 'We are the circumcision'), some are circumcised to God, and others are circumcised, yet not to God. There are also other words besides the word of truth, besides the word of the church. Those who philosophize chastise manners and the heart, and those from the heresies chastise, and circumcision happens for them. But it is circumcision, yet not to God; for circumcision happens among them by a false word.

But when according to the church's rule, according to the aim of sound teaching, you are in communion, you are not only circumcised—you are circumcised 'to God.' So 'Be circumcised to your God, and circumcise the foreskin of your heart.' (Philippians 3:21) Who does not pass these words by as clear? So there is a foreskin of the heart, and this must be circumcised.

The one who works the word carefully, searching such things in this place, will examine: foreskin is born with us; circumcision is acquired; and what has come from birth, circumcision removes. If then the word commands the foreskin of the heart to be removed, there must be something born with the heart which he calls foreskin, which must be removed so that someone may be circumcised as to the foreskin of the heart. If anyone understands, 'We were by nature children of wrath, like the rest' (Job 14:4; Prov 20:9); if anyone understands 'the body of our humiliation' in which we were born; if anyone understands, 'No one is clean from filth, not even if his life is one day; his months are numbered'—he will see how we were born with uncleanness and with the foreskin of our heart.
